description: The token-spelling contract (docs/contracts/token-spelling.md) for push. tickets: the host is application 'application' with push.ticket.key the current then the previous key of tickets.json (TEST KEYS), at 'now', with push.stream.max-lifetime 'maxLifetimeSeconds' and no proof key; the answer is 'valid', the reason the ticket grants nothing (the words of tickets.json), or 'malformed' (the subscribe answers 400 VALIDATION). streamTokens: verified with push.stream.secret 'streamSecret' (a TEST SECRET) at 'now'; the answer is 'valid' or the 401 code. Each value is one of conformance/push/issued-before.json (issued by the Go and the Java code before the rule), with every re-spelling ('respelled': contract section 3, the signature or MAC re-spelled every way, the other parts padded, whitespace and line breaks around the value), changes that certainly alter it ('tampered') and, for variants of the value whose parts take every residue mod 4, the signed parts re-spelled and signed again ('resigned': the signature or MAC is valid over the new text, so a lenient decoder would accept it), each with the answer it must get. Written by framework-push SpellingConformanceTest.
howToRun: Build the ticket keys and the stream-token verifier from the setup; check 'issued' and every case of 'respelled', 'tampered' and 'resigned' exactly as written (no trimming) and compare the answer with 'expect'.
